(text: 'str', *, library: 'str', file: 'str') -> 'list[Declaration]'
def extract_declarations(text: str, *, library: str, file: str) -> list[Declaration]:
    """Parse one Lean source into declarations. Heuristic, not a real parser."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    ns: list[str] = []
    pending_doc: str | None = None
    out: list[Declaration] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        stripped = lines[i].strip()
        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("/--"):
            doc, end = _read_docstring(lines, i)
            pending_doc = doc
            i = end + 1
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("/-"):  # module/section comment — skip the block
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and "-/" not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            i = j + 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("@["):  # attribute line — keep any pending docstring
            i += 1
            continue

        m_ns = _NAMESPACE_RE.match(stripped)
        if m_ns:
            ns.append(m_ns.group(1))
            pending_doc = None
            i += 1

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

 This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
 module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
 the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
 Grassmannian construction.

 properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.

 set_option autoImplicit false
 
 universe u
 
 open CategoryTheory Limits
 
 namespace AlgebraicGeometry
 
 namespace Scheme
 
 namespace DivFamily
 
 variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
 
 /-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
 family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
 projective twist. -/
 noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
   Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
 
 /-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
 noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
   (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
     Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
       ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
 
 /-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
 
 It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
 divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
 map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
 built into the definition. -/
 noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
       (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
   pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
       (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
     (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)

+proves. -/
+theorem grassmannianEval_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)

+  letI := hquot

+  infer_instance

 epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
 rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.

 uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
 finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
 outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
 -/

     [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
     (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
       ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
     LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T := by

     q := x.grassmannianEval L

     locFree := hLocFree }

 the Grassmannian representability theorem; well-definedness under

     [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
     (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
       ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :

 presentation.  Full faithfulness of `tilde` identifies that cokernel with the
 global-section module, without any noetherian hypothesis on `R`. -/

     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)
     [P.IsFinite] :
     Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := by
   let g := (tilde.functor R).preimage <|
     (tildeFinsupp _).hom ≫ P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _ ≫ (tildeFinsupp _).inv

     rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
     simpa only [LinearMap.range_eq_map] using Module.Finite.fg_top.map g.hom

 import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivPushforwardFlat
 import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GrassmannianRepresentability
 import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf
 
 /-!
 # The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
 
 This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
 module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
 the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
 Grassmannian construction.
 
 The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
 `DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
 epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
 uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
 comparison.
 
 The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
 pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
 `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
 their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
 properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
 -/
 
 set_option autoImplicit false
 
 universe u
 
 open CategoryTheory Limits
 
 namespace AlgebraicGeometry
 
 namespace Scheme
 
 namespace DivFamily
 
 variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
 
 /-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
 family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
 projective twist. -/
 noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
   Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
 
 /-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
 noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
   (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
     Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
       ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
 
 /-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
 
 It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
 divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
 map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
 built into the definition. -/
 noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
       (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
   pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
       (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
     (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)
 
+/-- **The conditional D2' quotient datum.**  Once the evaluation map is an
+epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
+rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.
+
+The two arguments are deliberately explicit: the evaluation map is the
+uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
+finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
+outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
+-/
+noncomputable def grassmannianQuotient (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
+    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
+    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
+      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
+    LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T := by
+  letI := hEpi
+  exact {
+    F := (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)
+    q := x.grassmannianEval L
+    epi := inferInstance
+    locFree := hLocFree }
+
+/-- The quotient-class value of the D2' comparison in the relative
+Grassmannian functor.  This is the representation-facing object consumed by
+the Grassmannian representability theorem; well-definedness under
+`DivFamily.Rel` is a separate comparison lemma. -/
+noncomputable def grassmannianClass (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
+    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
+    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
+      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
+    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
+  Quotient.mk _ (grassmannianQuotient L x hEpi hLocFree)
+
 end DivFamily
 
 namespace Modules
 
 set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
 /-- A finite global presentation of a module sheaf on `Spec R` induces a
 finite presentation of its module of global sections.
 
 The proof reconstructs the finite module cokernel underlying the sheaf
 presentation.  Full faithfulness of `tilde` identifies that cokernel with the
 global-section module, without any noetherian hypothesis on `R`. -/
 theorem module_finitePresentation_top_of_presentation
     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)
     [P.IsFinite] :
     Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := by
   let g := (tilde.functor R).preimage <|
     (tildeFinsupp _).hom ≫ P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _ ≫ (tildeFinsupp _).inv
   let Q := (P.generators.I →₀ R) ⧸ LinearMap.range g.hom
   have hQ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q := by
     apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective
       (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range g.hom)) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
     rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
     simpa only [LinearMap.range_eq_map] using Module.Finite.fg_top.map g.hom
   let iso : cokernel ((tilde.functor R).map g) ≅
       cokernel (P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _) := by
     refine cokernel.mapIso _ _ (tildeFinsupp _) (tildeFinsupp _) ?_
     simp only [g, (tilde.functor R).map_preimage]
     simp
   let eC : tilde (cokernel g) ≅ M :=
     PreservesCokernel.iso (tilde.functor R) g ≪≫ iso ≪≫
       IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _) P.isColimit
   let eQ : tilde (ModuleCat.of R Q) ≅ M :=
     (tilde.functor R).mapIso (ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient g).symm ≪≫ eC
   haveI : IsIso M.fromTildeΓ := isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_presentation M P
   let eΓ : ModuleCat.of R Q ≅ moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj M :=
     (tilde.functor R).preimageIso (eQ ≪≫ qcoh_iso_tilde_sections M)
   exact eΓ.toLinearEquiv.finitePresentation_iff.mp hQ
 
 /-- On an affine scheme, finite projective global sections of constant stalk
 rank produce the project-local rank-indexed freeness predicate used by the
 Grassmannian functor. -/
 theorem isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_finite_projective_sections
     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
     (hfin : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
     (hproj : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
     {d : ℕ} (hrank : ∀ t : PrimeSpectrum R, sectionsRankAtStalk M t = d) :
     SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank M d := by
   choose U htU hfree using fun t =>
     exists_free_restrict_of_finite_projective_sections' M hfin hproj t
   refine ⟨PrimeSpectrum R, U, ?_, fun t => ?_⟩
   · rw [eq_top_iff]
     intro t _
     exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨t, htU t⟩
   · exact (hrank t) ▸ hfree t
 
 end Modules
 
 end Scheme
 
 end AlgebraicGeometry

   432	\begin{proof}
   433	  By (ii) the structure map \(Z \to \Spec k\) is quasi-projective, hence
   434	  separated, so the first projection \(Z \times_k Z \to Z\) is separated.
   435	  By (iv) the first projection \(R \to Z\) is proper; it factors through
   436	  \(h : R \to Z \times_k Z\) over the diagonal embedding (the second
   437	  component is the second projection of \(R \to Z \times_P Z\)). The map
   438	  \(h\) is therefore proper, and a monomorphism (because \(R\) is the graph
   439	  of an equivalence relation on \(Z\), hence injective on \(T\)-points).
   440	  By EGA IV 8.11.5, a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion: \(h\) is a
   441	  closed embedding.
   442	
   443	  Hence \(R \hookrightarrow Z \times_k Z\) is a flat (by (iv)) and proper
   444	  equivalence relation on the quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\). By the
   445	  theory of flat-and-proper effective equivalence relations on
   446	  quasi-projective schemes (Altman--Kleiman; the construction places
   447	  the graph \(R \subseteq Z \times_k Z\) inside the universal subscheme of
   448	  the Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{Z/k}\) and descends to a closed subscheme
   449	  \(Q \subseteq \Hilb_{Z/k}\) representing the quotient), there exist a
   450	  quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Q\) and a faithfully flat, projective map
   451	  \(Z \to Q\) with \(R = Z \times_Q Z\).
   452	
   453	  The map \(Z \to Q\) is flat and proper; its fibers, up to field
   454	  extension, coincide with those of \(R \to Z\), which are smooth by
   455	  hypothesis. Hence \(Z \to Q\) is smooth.
   456	
   457	  Finally, \(Z \to Q\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves (an \'etale
   458	  cover of any \(T\)-point of \(Q\) pulls back to a \(T'\)-point of \(Z\), by
   459	  EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii) applied to \(Z \times_Q T \to T\)). In the category
   460	  of \'etale sheaves, both \(Q\) and \(P\) are coequalisers of the pair
   461	  \(R \rightrightarrows Z\); the coequaliser is unique up to unique
   462	  isomorphism, so \(Q\) represents \(P\). Smoothness of \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
   463	  is the smoothness of \(Z \to Q\) just shown.
   464	\end{proof}
   465	
   466	\begin{remark}[Quasi-projectivity is load-bearing]
   467	  \label{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}
   468	  \uses{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}
   469	  Hypothesis (ii) of \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient} --- that \(Z\) be
   470	  representable by a \emph{quasi-projective} \(k\)-scheme --- cannot be weakened
   471	  to bare representability. A Hironaka-type free \(\mathbb{Z}/2\)-action on a
   472	  smooth proper non-projective threefold gives a smooth proper equivalence
   473	  relation satisfying (i), (iii) and (iv) whose quotient \'etale sheaf is an
   474	  algebraic space and not a scheme.
   475	
   476	  This is what separates the two routes of \cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}. The
   477	  quotient route must supply quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice; the
   478	  Milne--Koll\'ar route quotients only by a finite Galois group, under the
   479	  hypothesis that every finite orbit lies in an affine open, which is a
   480	  condition the Hironaka example fails.
   481	\end{remark}

   483	\section{The Milne--Koll\'ar route}
   484	\label{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar}
   485	
   486	This section records the route of \cref{sec:fga_pic_setup} that avoids the
   487	quasi-projectivity obstruction of \cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis},
   488	in the three parts it decomposes into, and states the two of its inputs that are
   489	established.
   490	
   491	Over a separably closed field \(k'\) the construction is Milne \S 4. Fix
   492	\(r \ge 2g+1\) and a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme \(Z\). For a tuple \(\Sigma\) of
   493	\(r-g\) rational points of \(C' = C \times_k k'\), the locus
   494	\[
   495	  C^\Sigma
   496	    = \{\, t \in Z : h^0\bigl(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t\bigr) = 1 \,\}
   497	\]
   498	is open, because \(h^0\) is upper semicontinuous and \(h^0 \ge \chi = 1\) in
   499	degree \(g\); adding \(\Sigma\) back to the canonical divisor family of the
   500	rigidified pushforward gives a second map \(C^\Sigma \to Z\), and the equaliser
   501	\(J^\Sigma\) of the two represents the subfunctor of degree-\(r\) classes
   502	\(\mathcal{L}\) with \(h^0(\mathcal{L}(-\Sigma)_t) = 1\) at every point. These
   503	subfunctors cover, so gluing them represents \(\Pic^r_{C'/k'}\). Descent to
   504	\(k\) is a finite Galois quotient, and the degrees assemble as a coproduct over
   505	\(\mathbb{Z}\) through the translation isomorphisms
   506	\(\Pic^d \cong \Pic^r\) given by tensoring with \(\mathcal{O}((r-d) x_0)\).
   507	
   508	The two inputs the route rests on that the quotient route does not are the
   509	rigidified pushforward and the finite Galois quotient. The first is local freeness
   510	of \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) together with its compatibility with base change, and it
   511	holds for every curve satisfying the hypotheses of this chapter
   512	(\cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_gate}). The second is Speiser descent together with
   513	the existence of \(\Gamma\)-stable affine neighbourhoods.
   514	
   515	\begin{theorem}[Local freeness of the rigidified pushforward]\leanok
   516	  \label{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   517	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_proved}
   518	  \uses{lem:p1_integral}
   519	  \source{mumford-abelian-varieties:page-0054}
   520	  \textit{Source: [Mumford], \emph{Abelian Varieties}, II \S 5.}
   521	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\),
   522	  let \(A\) be a finitely generated \(k\)-algebra and \(q : C_A \to \Spec A\) the
   523	  constant family. Let \(\mathcal{L}\) be an invertible sheaf on \(C_A\) such that
   524	  for every point \(t\) of \(\Spec A\) some two-chart affine cover of the fibre
   525	  \(C_t\) has surjective {\v C}ech difference map on \(\mathcal{L}_t\) --- for a
   526	  separated fibre with affine chart intersection this computes
   527	  \(H^1(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t) = 0\). Then every point of \(\Spec A\) has an open
   528	  neighbourhood on which \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) is free of rank
   529	  \(h^0(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t)\).
   530	\end{theorem}
   531	
   532	\begin{remark}[Why the vanishing hypothesis is stated {\v C}ech-locally]
   533	  \label{rem:fiber_h1_vanishing_form}
   534	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   535	  The hypothesis of \cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free} asks for
   536	  \emph{some} two-chart cover of each fibre with surjective difference map,
   537	  rather than for vanishing of the sheaf cohomology \(H^1(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t)\).
   538	  On a separated fibre whose two charts have affine intersection the {\v C}ech
   539	  complex of that cover computes the sheaf cohomology, so the two agree; the
   540	  existential form is the weaker-looking one and is implied by any form of
   541	  \(h^1 = 0\), so a consumer supplying sheaf vanishing supplies this. The
   542	  identification is cover-independent by Mayer--Vietoris, but that
   543	  independence is not itself established here, which is why the hypothesis is
   544	  stated in the form that does not presuppose it.
   545	\end{remark}
   546	
   547	\begin{proof}\leanok
   548	  \uses{lem:p1_integral, thm:adelic_exists_finiteMorphismToP1}
   549	  Choose a finite morphism \(\pi : C \to \mathbb{P}^1_k\)
   550	  (\cref{thm:adelic_exists_finiteMorphismToP1}) and base change it to
   551	  \(\pi_A : C_A \to \mathbb{P}^1_A\). Since \(\pi_A\) is finite, it is affine and
   552	  \(\pi_{A*}\) is exact, so \(q_* \mathcal{L} = p_* (\pi_{A*} \mathcal{L})\) for
   553	  \(p : \mathbb{P}^1_A \to \Spec A\), and the fibrewise cohomology of
   554	  \(\pi_{A*}\mathcal{L}\) agrees with that of \(\mathcal{L}\).
   555	
   556	  On \(\mathbb{P}^1_A\) the two standard charts form an affine cover with affine
   557	  intersection, so the {\v C}ech complex of any quasi-coherent module is a
   558	  two-term complex \(d\) of \(\Gamma(\Spec A, \mathcal{O})\)-modules with
   559	  \(H^0 = \ker d\) and \(H^1 = \operatorname{coker} d\). Vanishing of \(H^1\) at
   560	  every point makes \(d\) surjective and \(\ker d\) finitely generated
   561	  projective, hence flat, and makes the formation of \(\ker d\) commute with
   562	  arbitrary base change; this is Mumford's two-term finite-free replacement.
   563	
   564	  Global sections of the pushforward are \(\ker d\) by the sheaf condition, so
   565	  \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) is finite locally free, and it remains to identify its
   566	  rank. Flatness gives
   567	  \(\operatorname{rank}_t = \dim_{\kappa(t)} \kappa(t) \otimes_A \ker d\), base
   568	  change moves the residue field inside the kernel, and comparing the
   569	  \(\kappa(t)\)-base-changed {\v C}ech square with the {\v C}ech square of the
   570	  fibre identifies that dimension with \(h^0(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t)\). A finite
   571	  locally free module of locally constant rank is free on a neighbourhood of each
   572	  point.
   573	\end{proof}

   575	\begin{lemma}[Global sections of the pushforward commute with base change]\leanok
   576	  \label{lem:gamma_base_change}
   577	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.rigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange_proved}
   578	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   579	  In the situation of \cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}, for every ring
   580	  map \(A \to A'\) --- with no finiteness, flatness or noetherian hypothesis on
   581	  \(A'\) --- the canonical map
   582	  \[
   583	    A' \otimes_A \Gamma(C_A, \mathcal{L})
   584	      \longrightarrow \Gamma(C_{A'}, g'^* \mathcal{L})
   585	  \]
   586	  is bijective.
   587	\end{lemma}
   588	
   589	\begin{proof}\leanok
   590	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   591	  Push forward along the finite \(\pi_A : C_A \to \mathbb{P}^1_A\) as in
   592	  \cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free} and work with the two-term {\v C}ech
   593	  complex \(d\) of the preimage cover. Fibrewise vanishing of \(H^1\) makes \(d\)
   594	  surjective, and for a surjective two-term complex the formation of \(\ker d\)
   595	  is universally exact: base changing the short exact sequence
   596	  \(0 \to \ker d \to K^0 \to K^1 \to 0\) along \(A \to A'\) stays exact because
   597	  \(K^1\) is flat, so \(A' \otimes_A \ker d \to \ker(d \otimes A')\) is
   598	  bijective. Global sections of the pushforward are \(\ker d\) on both sides by
   599	  the sheaf condition, which gives the claim.
   600	\end{proof}
   601	
   602	\begin{theorem}[The rigidified pushforward exists for every curve]\leanok
   603	  \label{thm:rigid_pushforward_gate}
   604	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve}
   605	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free, lem:gamma_base_change}
   606	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\).
   607	  Then \(C\) admits the rigidified pushforward: for every finitely generated
   608	  \(k\)-algebra \(A\) and every invertible sheaf on \(C_A\) with fibrewise
   609	  vanishing \(H^1\), the pushforward \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) is locally free of rank
   610	  \(h^0\) of the fibre and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change.
   611	\end{theorem}
   612	
   613	\begin{proof}\leanok
   614	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free, lem:gamma_base_change}
   615	  The two conclusions are \cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free} and, by
   616	  affine-target descent from the module-level statement of
   617	  \cref{lem:gamma_base_change}, the base-change conclusion: over an affine base
   618	  both ends of the adjunction mate are quasi-coherent, and a morphism of
   619	  quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme is an isomorphism as soon as it is
   620	  bijective on global sections.
   621	\end{proof}

   623	\begin{lemma}[The projective line over a field is integral]\leanok
   624	  \label{lem:p1_integral}
   625	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isIntegral_p1_of_isDomain_charts}
   626	  Let \(k\) be a field. Then \(\mathbb{P}^1_k\) is an integral scheme.

   629	\begin{proof}\leanok
   630	  Each standard chart \(V_i \subseteq \mathbb{P}^1_k\) is affine with section
   631	  ring the polynomial ring \(k[T]\) in the chart coordinate, hence an integral
   632	  domain, so each chart is an integral scheme. Reducedness of \(\mathbb{P}^1_k\)
   633	  follows because the two charts cover and reducedness is local. For
   634	  irreducibility, the overlap \(W = V_0 \cap V_1\) is a nonempty open subset of
   635	  the irreducible \(V_0\), hence irreducible and dense in \(V_0\), and
   636	  symmetrically dense in \(V_1\); as \(V_0 \cup V_1 = \mathbb{P}^1_k\), the set
   637	  \(W\) is a dense irreducible subset of \(\mathbb{P}^1_k\), which is therefore
   638	  the closure of an irreducible set and so irreducible.
   639	\end{proof}

   641	\begin{theorem}[Speiser descent]\leanok
   642	  \label{thm:speiser_descent}
   643	  \lean{AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction.descentAlgEquiv}
   644	  Let \(L/K\) be a finite Galois extension with group \(\Gamma\), and let \(A\)
   645	  be an \(L\)-algebra carrying an action of \(\Gamma\) by ring automorphisms
   646	  which is semilinear over the action of \(\Gamma\) on \(L\). Then the canonical
   647	  map
   648	  \[
   649	    L \otimes_K A^\Gamma \longrightarrow A, \qquad a \otimes w \mapsto a w,
   650	  \]
   651	  is an isomorphism of \(L\)-algebras: the invariants form a \(K\)-form of
   652	  \(A\). No finiteness hypothesis on \(A\) is required.
   653	\end{theorem}
   654	
   655	\begin{proof}\leanok
   656	  The same statement for semilinear \(\Gamma\)-modules is the classical
   657	  normal-basis argument: writing \(L = K[\Gamma] \cdot \theta\) for a normal
   658	  basis element \(\theta\), the trace \(\sum_{\gamma} \gamma(\theta a) \gamma\)
   659	  exhibits every element of \(A\) as an \(L\)-combination of invariants, and
   660	  \(L\)-independence of the invariant part follows from linear independence of
   661	  the characters \(\gamma\). The map above is the \(L\)-algebra map extending the
   662	  inclusion \(A^\Gamma \hookrightarrow A\), and its underlying additive map is
   663	  the module-level descent map, which the module statement shows bijective.
   664	  Bijectivity of an algebra homomorphism makes it an algebra isomorphism.
   665	\end{proof}

   667	\begin{theorem}[Points of the finite Galois quotient]\leanok
   668	  \label{thm:galois_quotient_points}
   669	  \lean{AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction.invariantAlgHomEquiv}
   670	  \uses{thm:speiser_descent}

   672	  the map \(g \mapsto (\mathrm{id}_L \otimes g)\) is a bijection
   673	  \[
   674	    \mathrm{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(A^\Gamma, B)
   675	      \;\simeq\;
   676	    \{\, f \in \mathrm{Hom}_{L\text{-alg}}(A, L \otimes_K B) :
   677	       f(\gamma \cdot x) = (\gamma \otimes \mathrm{id})(f(x)) \,\}.
   678	  \]

   680	  \(\Spec A^\Gamma\) are the \(\Gamma\)-equivariant \(T_L\)-points of
   681	  \(\Spec A\): the affine scheme \(\Spec A^\Gamma\) is the quotient of
   682	  \(\Spec A\) by \(\Gamma\).

   686	  \uses{thm:speiser_descent}

   688	  \(A \cong L \otimes_K A^\Gamma\) of \cref{thm:speiser_descent}; equivariance is
   689	  the identity \(\gamma \otimes \mathrm{id}\) transported along the same
   690	  isomorphism, which is exactly the compatibility recorded there. Conversely, an
   691	  equivariant \(f\) carries invariants to \(\Gamma\)-fixed elements of
   692	  \(L \otimes_K B\), and for the left-factor action on a base change the fixed

   695	  is the computation of the restriction on invariants, and the other holds
   696	  because the invariants span \(A\) over \(L\), so two \(L\)-algebra maps
   697	  agreeing on them agree.

   701	  \label{lem:stable_affine_open}
   702	  \lean{AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen}
   703	  \uses{thm:galois_quotient_points}
   704	  Let \(L/K\) be finite Galois with group \(\Gamma\) and let \(X\) be a scheme
   705	  over \(L\) with a semilinear \(\Gamma\)-action all of whose orbits are
   706	  contained in affine opens. Then every point of \(X\) has a \(\Gamma\)-stable
   707	  affine open neighbourhood.
   708	\end{lemma}
   709	
   710	\begin{proof}\leanok
   711	  Let \(x \in X\) and let \(U\) be an affine open containing the orbit of \(x\).
   712	  The orbit is finite and lies in the open
   713	  \(W = \bigcap_{\gamma} \gamma^{-1} U\), so by prime avoidance inside the affine
   714	  \(U\) there is a section \(s \in \Gamma(X, U)\) with the whole orbit contained
   715	  in \(D(s) \subseteq W\). Put \(N = \prod_{\gamma} \gamma(s)|_W\). Then
   716	  \(D(N) = \bigcap_{\gamma} \gamma^{-1} D(s)\), which contains \(x\) because the
   717	  orbit lies in \(D(s)\), and is \(\Gamma\)-stable because translating the
   718	  intersection permutes its factors. Finally \(D(N) \subseteq D(s)\) by the
   719	  factor \(\gamma = 1\), so \(D(N)\) is a basic open of the affine \(D(s)\) and
   720	  hence affine.
   721	\end{proof}

     5	\section{Setup and motivation}
     6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
     7	
     8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
     9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
    10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
    11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
    12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
    13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
    14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
    15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
    16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
    17	
    18	\medskip
    19	
    20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
    21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
    22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
    23	
    24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
    25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
    26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
    27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
    28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
    29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
    30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
    31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. It is the route of
    32	the proof written out under \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} below.
    33	
    34	That attribution needs one qualification, or the reader takes the chapter's headline
    35	theorem for a construction it is not. Neither route is carried out in full here:
    36	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} is a statement \emph{about} the existence predicate
    37	of \cref{def:has_pic_scheme}, from which it extracts the representing property, and the
    38	one assertion of this chapter that is not proved is
    39	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale} --- a bare \texttt{sorry} in Lean, from which
    40	the \(\Pic^\sharp\)-shaped predicate \cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme} is
    41	\emph{derived} rather than assumed. \Cref{rem:representability_is_conditional} states this
    42	precisely.
    43	So "the route of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}" names the argument its proof
    44	records, not a discharge of the predicate --- and the choice of route below is a choice
    45	about which argument is being built out, not about which theorem is available today.
    46	
    47	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
    48	separably closed field, from the open loci
    49	\[
    50	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
    51	\]
    52	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
    53	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
    54	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
    55	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
    56	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme. Its structure, and the parts of it that
    57	are established, are the subject of \cref{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar}.
    58	
    59	The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
    60	quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
    61	the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
    62	(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
    63	only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
    64	that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
    65	Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
    66	mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
    67	consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
    68	
    69	\medskip
    70	
    71	\textbf{The functor being represented: the \'etale sheafification.} Kleiman \S 4
    72	represents the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), and that is the
    73	formulation this project realises: representability is asserted for
    74	\(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) over an \emph{arbitrary} base field, with \emph{no}
    75	hypothesis on \(C(k)\) (\cref{def:pic_et_sheaf},
    76	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale}).
    77	
    78	The reason is not a preference between equivalent options. An unconditional
    79	representability statement for \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) is not merely unproved but
    80	\emph{false}: Kleiman L5105--L5108 exhibits the conic \(u^2+v^2+w^2=0\) in
    81	\(\I P^2_\bb R\) --- a smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically
    82	integral over a field with no rational point --- for which \(\Pic_{X/\bb R}\) is
    83	not representable while \(\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\et}\) is.
    84	
    85	\emph{Corrected} (2026-07-29, \texttt{review-ajc}). This paragraph previously gave
    86	the reason as: \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) ``is not a sheaf for any topology in general
    87	--- not even the Zariski one'', with representability of a functor forcing the
    88	sheaf condition for every subcanonical topology. The second half is right, but no
    89	source supports the first for the \emph{relative} functor: \texttt{th:cmp} part 1
    90	gives \(\Pic_{X/S}\into\Pic_{(X/S)\zar}\) whenever
    91	\(\mc O_{\!S}\risom f_*\mc O_{\!X}\) holds universally, so on these hypotheses it
    92	is Zariski-\emph{separated}. Take the non-representability directly instead; in
    93	Lean it is
    94	\texttt{PicScheme.not\_exists\_representing\_picSharp\_of\_not\_isIso}, whose only
    95	open input is that the comparison really fails for that conic. Sheafifying repairs this by construction; a rational point repairs
    96	it by hypothesis, and the resulting theorem is about a smaller class of curves.
    97	
    98	\medskip
    99	
   100	\textbf{What a rational point buys, and why it is kept.} Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5
   101	(\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
   102	and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
   103	(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
   104	base change), then the comparison maps
   105	\[
   106	  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
   107	  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
   108	\]
   109	are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under a rational-point hypothesis the
   110	plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, and one may work directly
   111	with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
   112	
   113	So there are two formulations, and they prove different theorems.
   114	
   115	\begin{enumerate}
   116	  \item \textbf{The one realised.} Represent the \'etale sheafification
   117	    \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) (\cref{def:pic_et_sheaf}) and carry no hypothesis on
   118	    \(C(k)\). This is Kleiman's own formulation, and it needs no section
   119	    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
   120	    would have supplied globally. It is the statement of
   121	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale}, and it is what the Jacobian
   122	    headline (\cref{chap:Jacobian}) rests on.
   123	  \item \textbf{Retained, and strictly weaker.} Represent
   124	    \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis.
   125	    This is the formulation of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of the
   126	    \(\Pic^\sharp\)-shaped assertions later in this chapter. It is strictly
   127	    weaker than a statement about all smooth proper geometrically integral
   128	    curves, since such a curve need not have a rational point --- a conic
   129	    without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no
   130	    rational point, satisfies every other hypothesis. It is retained because it
   131	    is true and because the tangent-space development is written against the
   132	    \(\Pic^\sharp\) shape, and it may not be presented as the project's
   133	    headline.
   134	\end{enumerate}
   135	
   136	Which formulation to target was a decision about what theorem is being claimed,
   137	not a limitation of the platform, and it is \emph{settled}: formulation (1), by
   138	owner decision of 2026-07-28. What follows from that decision, and is worth
   139	stating because a reader of the later sections will meet the
   140	\(\Pic^\sharp\)-shaped statements first: those sections' rational-point
   141	hypothesis is now the mark of a conditional milestone rather than a standing
   142	convention of the chapter. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
   143	\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies the section they need.

   149	\section{Line bundles and the Quot / Hilbert scheme}
   150	\label{sec:fga_pic_line_bundle_quot}
   151	
   152	The bridge from line bundles on \(C \times_k T\) to the Quot scheme is the
   153	Abel map: a relative effective divisor \(D \subset C \times_k T\) over \(T\)
   154	(a \(T\)-flat closed subscheme whose ideal is invertible) determines a closed
   155	subscheme of \(C \times_k T\) flat over \(T\), hence a \(T\)-point of the Hilbert
   156	functor \(\Hilb_{C/k}(T)\), which is the special case \(\Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\)
   157	of the Quot functor of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}; and it determines an
   158	invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\) on the relative curve,
   159	representing a class in \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T)\).

   184	  target and invertible kernel. The second transformation is pointwise

   317	\begin{proof}

   319	  We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
   320	  \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
   321	  comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of

   323	  \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
   324	  correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.

   326	  \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
   327	  By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
   328	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}

   357	  \(k\)-scheme.
   358	
   359	  \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}

   361	  of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
   362	  is representable by an open subscheme of \(\Hilb_{C/k}\) (and hence by an
   363	  open subscheme of the Quot scheme of \cref{thm:quot_representable}), and
   364	  is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along
   365	  \(P^{\phi_0}_0 \hookrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) yields an open
   366	  subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi_0}_0 \times_{\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
   367	  of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection
   368	  \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi_0}_0\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves:
   369	  given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda\) of \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) represented by an \'etale
   370	  cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times_k
   371	  T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle
   372	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to
   373	  \(\mathcal{Q} := \pi_{T'*}\mathcal{L}'\) is smooth over \(T'\); an \'etale
   374	  cover \(T_1 \to T'\) admits a \(T'\)-map \(T_1 \to \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q})\)
   375	  (EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii)) whose composition with the universal divisor map
   376	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to Z\) produces the required \(T_1\)-point of \(Z\).
   377	  Moreover, the first projection \(Z \times_{P^{\phi_0}_0} Z \to Z\) is
   378	  smooth and proper.
   379	
   380	  \emph{Step 4: descend by the smooth-proper quotient lemma.}
   381	  Apply Kleiman~\S 4, Lem.~4.9: given a surjection \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
   382	  of \'etale sheaves with \(Z\) quasi-projective, \(R := Z \times_P Z\)
   383	  representable, and the first projection \(R \to Z\) smooth and proper,
   384	  \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective scheme. In our case
   385	  \(P = P^{\phi_0}_0\), \(Z\) and \(R\) as above, so \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) is
   386	  quasi-projective. Reassembling over \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\) and

   388	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\). The total scheme is separated (as a disjoint
   389	  union of separated quasi-projectives) and locally of finite type. This
   390	  is Kleiman~\S 4, Cor.~4.18.3 in the \(S = \Spec k\),
   391	  \(X = C\) complete case.
   392	\end{proof}

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.IsTerminal
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Basic

/-!
# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object

This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".

Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
presheaves.

## Why it is worth a named declaration

`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.

## The intended consumer

`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
divisor). If a lane proves the matching
`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
`representableByTerminal` yields
`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
the categorical interface it plugs into.

Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
-/

universe w v u

namespace CategoryTheory.Functor

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
any terminal object.**

The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.

This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    F.RepresentableBy Y where
  homEquiv {X} := by
    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    exact
      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
terminal object represents it. -/
noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)

/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    F.IsRepresentable :=
  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable

end CategoryTheory.Functor

+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.IsTerminal
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Basic
+
+/-!
+# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object
+
+This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
+`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
+"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".
+
+Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
+`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
+`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
+statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
+build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
+the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
+and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
+mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
+`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
+presheaves.
+
+## Why it is worth a named declaration
+
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
+naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
+subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
+still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
+it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
+`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
+single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.
+
+## The intended consumer
+
+`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
+for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
+divisor). If a lane proves the matching
+`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
+*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
+`representableByTerminal` yields
+`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
+genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
+is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
+infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
+the categorical interface it plugs into.
+
+Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
+hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
+-/
+
+universe v u
+
+namespace CategoryTheory.Functor
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
+
+/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
+any terminal object.**
+
+The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
+unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
+exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
+are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.
+
+This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
+absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y where
+  homEquiv {X} := by
+    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact
+      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
+        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
+        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
+        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
+  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
+
+/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
+of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
+terminal object represents it. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
+  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)
+
+/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
+representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
+theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.IsRepresentable :=
+  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable
+
+end CategoryTheory.Functor

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`
— so a read-only reviewer cannot edit source. Every subagent (read-only or not)
can still file issues/memory and write its report via the `horizon inbox` CLI;
that is how read-only agents act. The descriptor's `write_domain` documents what
a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

## Model and effort — the Horizon agent owns the spend

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.

  "title": "Review and macro lane on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge: verify real progress and source faithfulness",
  "objective": "You are the REVIEW and MACRO lane on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge. You do not race the provers for declarations. Your job is to make sure their work is real, correctly aimed, and faithful to the sources.\n\nSCOPE: you may read anything, file inbox issues, and correct roadmap rows and blueprint prose. Do NOT edit Lean proofs \u2014 the provers own those files and you share one git index with them. If you find a wrong Lean statement, file it as an issue at the site and DM the owning lane.\n\nWHAT TO CHECK, in rough priority order:\n\n1. IS THERE REAL PROGRESS? Measure, do not read reports. The metric that matters is producers vs consumers of an unproduced hypothesis: `rep` (RepresentableBy) has ~0 producers in AJC and 7 in AJCR against ~35 and ~96 consumers. A lane that adds consumers is not advancing the headline. Report these counts at HEAD vs the run's base commit, and name any lane whose net contribution is new consumers.\n\n2. IS THE MATHEMATICS FAITHFUL TO THE REFERENCES? references/ holds Kleiman, Hartshorne, FGA-explained, Milne, abelian-varieties and more. Check that roadmap and blueprint statements match the cited source \u2014 same hypotheses, not just the same conclusion. CONVENTIONS ARE THE TRAP: projective vs proper, ample vs very ample, integral vs irreducible vs reduced, k-rational vs closed point, relative vs absolute. A theorem imported under the wrong convention is a hallucination that typechecks nowhere and blocks everything downstream. A cited lemma is absent unless it is in the citing file's import closure \u2014 grep cannot see that difference, so #check it.\n\n3. IS THE CHOSEN PATH RELEVANT? The headline is Picard/Pic^0 representability. For each active row ask what discharging it buys the headline.      6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivPushforwardFlat
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GrassmannianRepresentability
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
    12	
    13	This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
    14	module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
    15	the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
    16	Grassmannian construction.
    17	
    18	The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
    19	`DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
    20	epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
    21	uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
    22	comparison.
    23	
    24	The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
    25	pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
    26	`Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
    27	their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
    28	properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	set_option autoImplicit false
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits
    36	
    37	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    38	
    39	namespace Scheme
    40	
    41	namespace DivFamily
    42	
    43	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
    44	
    45	/-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
    46	family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
    47	projective twist. -/
    48	noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    49	    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
    50	  Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
    51	
    52	/-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
    53	noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    54	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=

 import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GrassmannianRepresentability
 import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf
 
 /-!
 # The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
 
 This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
 module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
 the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
 Grassmannian construction.
 
 The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
 `DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
 epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
 uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
 comparison.
 
 The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
 pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
 `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
 their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
 properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
 -/
 
 set_option autoImplicit false
 
 universe u
 
 open CategoryTheory Limits
 
 namespace AlgebraicGeometry
 
 namespace Scheme
 
 namespace DivFamily
 
 variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
 
 /-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
 family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
 projective twist. -/
 noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
   Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
 
 /-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
 noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
   (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
     Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
       ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)

 divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
 map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
 built into the definition. -/
 noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
       (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
   pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
       (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
     (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)

+This keeps the base-change and divisor-quotient obligations separate, so a
+later uniform-generation proof can discharge only the factor it actually
+proves. -/
+theorem grassmannianEval_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)

+      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))

+      (x.twistQuotientMap L))) :

+  letI := hbase
+  letI := hquot
+  dsimp [grassmannianEval]
+  infer_instance

 epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
 rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.

 uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
 finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
 outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
 -/

     [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
     (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
       ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :

 `DivFamily.Rel` is a separate comparison lemma. -/

     [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
     (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
       ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
     (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
   Quotient.mk _ (grassmannianQuotient L x hEpi hLocFree)

+divisor-quotient factors are epi, only the target's rank condition remains. -/
+noncomputable def grassmannianClassOfComponents (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
+    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}

+    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
+      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
+    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=

 namespace Modules
 
 set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in

 finite presentation of its module of global sections.

 presentation.  Full faithfulness of `tilde` identifies that cokernel with the
 global-section module, without any noetherian hypothesis on `R`. -/

     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)
     [P.IsFinite] :
     Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := by
   let g := (tilde.functor R).preimage <|
     (tildeFinsupp _).hom ≫ P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _ ≫ (tildeFinsupp _).inv
   let Q := (P.generators.I →₀ R) ⧸ LinearMap.range g.hom
   have hQ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q := by
     apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective
       (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range g.hom)) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
     rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
     simpa only [LinearMap.range_eq_map] using Module.Finite.fg_top.map g.hom

       cokernel (P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _) := by
     refine cokernel.mapIso _ _ (tildeFinsupp _) (tildeFinsupp _) ?_
     simp only [g, (tilde.functor R).map_preimage]
     simp

       IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _) P.isColimit

     (tilde.functor R).mapIso (ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient g).symm ≪≫ eC

   let eΓ : ModuleCat.of R Q ≅ moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj M :=
     (tilde.functor R).preimageIso (eQ ≪≫ qcoh_iso_tilde_sections M)
   exact eΓ.toLinearEquiv.finitePresentation_iff.mp hQ

 Grassmannian functor. -/

     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
     (hfin : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
     (hproj : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
     {d : ℕ} (hrank : ∀ t : PrimeSpectrum R, sectionsRankAtStalk M t = d) :
     SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank M d := by
   choose U htU hfree using fun t =>
     exists_free_restrict_of_finite_projective_sections' M hfin hproj t
   refine ⟨PrimeSpectrum R, U, ?_, fun t => ?_⟩
   · rw [eq_top_iff]
     intro t _
     exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨t, htU t⟩
   · exact (hrank t) ▸ hfree t
 
 end Modules
 
 end Scheme
 
 end AlgebraicGeometry

     {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)

   432	\begin{proof}
   433	  By (ii) the structure map \(Z \to \Spec k\) is quasi-projective, hence
   434	  separated, so the first projection \(Z \times_k Z \to Z\) is separated.
   435	  By (iv) the first projection \(R \to Z\) is proper; it factors through
   436	  \(h : R \to Z \times_k Z\) over the diagonal embedding (the second
   437	  component is the second projection of \(R \to Z \times_P Z\)). The map
   438	  \(h\) is therefore proper, and a monomorphism (because \(R\) is the graph
   439	  of an equivalence relation on \(Z\), hence injective on \(T\)-points).
   440	  By EGA IV 8.11.5, a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion: \(h\) is a
   441	  closed embedding.
   442	
   443	  Hence \(R \hookrightarrow Z \times_k Z\) is a flat (by (iv)) and proper
   444	  equivalence relation on the quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\). By the
   445	  theory of flat-and-proper effective equivalence relations on
   446	  quasi-projective schemes (Altman--Kleiman; the construction places
   447	  the graph \(R \subseteq Z \times_k Z\) inside the universal subscheme of
   448	  the Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{Z/k}\) and descends to a closed subscheme
   449	  \(Q \subseteq \Hilb_{Z/k}\) representing the quotient), there exist a
   450	  quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Q\) and a faithfully flat, projective map
   451	  \(Z \to Q\) with \(R = Z \times_Q Z\).
   452	
   453	  The map \(Z \to Q\) is flat and proper; its fibers, up to field
   454	  extension, coincide with those of \(R \to Z\), which are smooth by
   455	  hypothesis. Hence \(Z \to Q\) is smooth.
   456	
   457	  Finally, \(Z \to Q\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves (an \'etale
   458	  cover of any \(T\)-point of \(Q\) pulls back to a \(T'\)-point of \(Z\), by
   459	  EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii) applied to \(Z \times_Q T \to T\)). In the category
   460	  of \'etale sheaves, both \(Q\) and \(P\) are coequalisers of the pair
   461	  \(R \rightrightarrows Z\); the coequaliser is unique up to unique
   462	  isomorphism, so \(Q\) represents \(P\). Smoothness of \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
   463	  is the smoothness of \(Z \to Q\) just shown.
   464	\end{proof}

   466	\begin{remark}[Quasi-projectivity is load-bearing]
   467	  \label{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}
   468	  \uses{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}
   469	  Hypothesis (ii) of \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient} --- that \(Z\) be
   470	  representable by a \emph{quasi-projective} \(k\)-scheme --- cannot be weakened
   471	  to bare representability. A Hironaka-type free \(\mathbb{Z}/2\)-action on a
   472	  smooth proper non-projective threefold gives a smooth proper equivalence
   473	  relation satisfying (i), (iii) and (iv) whose quotient \'etale sheaf is an
   474	  algebraic space and not a scheme.
   475	
   476	  This is what separates the two routes of \cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}. The
   477	  quotient route must supply quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice; the
   478	  Milne--Koll\'ar route quotients only by a finite Galois group, under the
   479	  hypothesis that every finite orbit lies in an affine open, which is a
   480	  condition the Hironaka example fails.
   481	\end{remark}
